headline: Red Sox sweep the twin bill as we eye October
morning_brew: What a hell of a day at Fenway. We took both ends of the doubleheader from the Cubs, and that is exactly the kind of electric momentum we needed to keep the Duck Boat fund alive. In the opener, Roman Anthony led the way with three hits, while the bullpen held the line to squeak out a one-run victory that took three years off my life. Then in the nightcap, Wilyer Abreu delivered a two-run double in the eighth inning to provide all the offense Jedixson Paez needed to shut the door. Seeing the squad battle like that through eighteen innings tells me we have the heart to make some serious noise when we head up to New York.

The Bruins are leaving a sour taste in my mouth, falling to the Capitals in overtime last night. Jeremy Swayman kept us in it with thirty-two saves, but we just could not solve the Caps when it mattered most. Morgan Geekie and David Pastrnak found the back of the net, but giving up that OT goal so quickly is a tough pill to swallow this early in the preseason. My neighbor Rick is already drafting another one of his endless, unhinged grievances to the league about the flow of the game, and I might just sign it with him this time because the officiating was an absolute disaster.

We close out the series against the Cubs on Sunday in Florida, and then the real business begins against the Yankees. Sully keeps insisting we are saving our best baseball for the postseason, and for once, I really hope he is right. We have a busy stretch ahead, but at least we are heading into the final push with our heads held high after sweeping that twin bill. Let us hope the flight down to St. Petersburg is smooth and we finish this regular season on a high note.

trend_watch.dans_take: That is how you step up and earn your dinner when the starter leaves you hanging.

trend_watch.dans_take: He is basically playing goalie for a team that keeps leaving him on an island.
